title: VvMYBC2-L1 cooperates with histone deacetylase VvHDA15 to repress anthocyanin biosynthesis in grape under high temperature
content:
Abstract
High temperature restricts anthocyanin accumulation in grape berries, but how transcriptional repressors coordinate with chromatin regulation remains unclear. We identified the MYB repressor VvMYBC2-L1 as a heat-responsive regulator through transcriptome analysis and functional assays. VvMYBC2-L1 overexpression reduced berry and callus pigmentation, anthocyanin accumulation, and expression of phenylpropanoid and anthocyanin biosynthetic genes. VvMYBC2-L1 associated with selected VvPAL and VvUFGT promoter regions, interacted with the basic helix-loop-helix protein VvMYC1, weakened the VvMYBA1–VvMYC1 interaction, and reduced their activation of both promoters. VvMYBC2-L1 also directly interacted with VvHDA15, a nuclear class II histone deacetylase with enzymatic activity in vitro. VvHDA15 overexpression repressed anthocyanin accumulation and reduced histone H3 lysine 9 acetylation at selected VvPAL and VvUFGT promoter regions. Conversely, VvHDA15 silencing partially restored berry coloration and anthocyanin accumulation under high temperature. Co-expression of VvMYBC2-L1 and VvHDA15 strengthened repression of anthocyanin accumulation and target-gene expression and further reduced histone acetylation at selected promoter regions relative to VvHDA15 overexpression alone. These findings identify functional cooperation between a heat-responsive MYB repressor and histone deacetylation that limits anthocyanin biosynthesis in grape berries.
